_comment: The engine-gap ledger: plugin state shapes the generic grammar could not represent, typed so demand is COUNTABLE. tools/engine-gap-doc.php projects docs/guides/adapter-authoring-limitations.md from this file and `make release-gate` byte-compares the result, so the prose and the data cannot disagree. `primitives` is a CLOSED vocabulary -- the projector refuses a coordinate naming a primitive that is not declared here, and refuses a declared primitive nothing demands. That closure is the whole point: two candidates blocked on the same missing thing must name the SAME primitive id, so the open-demand ranking counts one primitive with two candidates rather than two lookalike wishlist lines. Adding a row is a review act, not a note-to-self: every `closed_by`/`evidence` path is checked to exist on disk, so a closed gap whose implementation moved fails the gate instead of quietly becoming a claim about nothing. CLOSURE IS PER COORDINATE (WP-6.1): `closed_by` sits on the coordinate whose primitive shipped, and a candidate's `disposition` is derived from its coordinates and merely checked -- `closed` exactly when every one of them carries `closed_by`. WP-6.1 forced that split by shipping a primitive that unblocked part of a row and none of the rest, which row-level closure could only state as one of two false sentences.

structured_post_body_reference_paths.title: structured post-body reference paths
structured_post_body_reference_paths.definition: Addressing a reference inside a post BODY by a declared path, so a source-local id embedded in structured post_content is rebound rather than carried over verbatim. Shipped as the `json` post-type body mode plus the top-level `body_refs` section, both gated on the engine feature `structured-body-refs/v1` (spec/repo-format.md § v3.20). The path dialect is the shipped `json_refs` one, unchanged; what the primitive adds beside it is the identity round-trip precondition over the whole document, the per-path declared JSON type, and the declared `sentinels` literal set that keeps a non-reference value at a reference path a refusal rather than a guess.

type_preserving_string_id_attr_codec.title: a type-preserving string-id attribute codec
type_preserving_string_id_attr_codec.definition: A block/shortcode attribute codec that resolves an entity id and writes it back in the JSON type it was stored as, instead of normalising every id to an integer.

taxonomy_delete_scope_exercise.title: a complete taxonomy/delete-scope exercise
taxonomy_delete_scope_exercise.definition: The adversarial matrix that must run before a post-type adapter carrying an authored taxonomy may claim a deletion selector: term-attached state, cascade scope, and residue on a dirty target.

serialized_column_codec.title: structured typed-table column codecs that decode, tokenize string leaves, and re-encode canonical PHP serialization
serialized_column_codec.definition: A typed-table column codec that round-trips a PHP-serialized container: decode, tokenize the string leaves, re-encode with correct length prefixes. Distinct from structured_leaf_text_codec because the re-encode half is the hazard -- a tokenized string of a different byte length invalidates the serialization.

verified_provider_postcondition.title: a provider whose success is a bounded, verified postcondition rather than an exit-code-only callback
verified_provider_postcondition.definition: Direct writes bypass the side effects a plugin's own save path performs (cache drops, rewrite flushes, execution-file rebuilds). Apply cannot be claimed on a plugin with such a side effect until a provider both performs it and PROVES it, because an exit code proves only that something ran.

structured_leaf_text_codec.title: an explicit structured-leaf text codec independent of fake reference paths
structured_leaf_text_codec.definition: Tokenizing the string leaves of a nested array-valued option that declares no reference, without inventing a reference path to reach them.

post_apply_registration_boundary.title: a verified post-apply type-registration/process boundary
post_apply_registration_boundary.definition: A stated, verified boundary for state that a plugin consumes during `init`: applied definitions do not exist in the process that wrote them, so entity materialization depending on them must be sequenced across processes rather than assumed.

dynamic_option_name_reference_rule.title: a generic dynamic derived option-name reference rule
dynamic_option_name_reference_rule.definition: Widens the shipped `option_name_refs` rule, which captures a numeric ROW id out of the option name, to a name whose dynamic segment is a slug and whose VALUE is the local reference.

table_scoped_cache_entry_invalidation.title: a cache entry shared by every row of a table, dropped once per apply rather than per row
table_scoped_cache_entry_invalidation.definition: An object-cache entry whose key and group are both literal -- no `{id}` anywhere -- so it is ONE entry the whole table shares rather than one per row. The per-row `{cache_group, cache_key}` verb requires `{id}` in one member and therefore refuses it: with no substitution point every row of the table would name the same entry. This stays recorded rather than admitted because it has exactly ONE demand, which is the same admission rule that let `row_cache_entry_invalidation` in on two. The blanket case was already reviewed into the top-level `actions` channel (manifests/woocommerce.json:307), but that channel has an engine-owned native action for a transient and none for the object cache, so a plugin-owned cache group is still reachable only through a provider.

composite_ref_identity.title: join-table identity with no scalar primary key (`identity.mode: composite_ref`)
composite_ref_identity.definition: A pure join table's identity is its two reference columns, not a row id: every identity column is a ref and every ref is an identity column.

option_name_refs.title: an option-name reference rule binding a numeric row id captured from the option NAME
option_name_refs.definition: A top-level `option_name_refs` list whose anchored `match` regex carries exactly one named `(?<id>...)` capture bound to a table id_kind, driving its own name-scan discovery pass.

row_cache_invalidation.title: a per-row `invalidate` declaration that drops a plugin's own derived cache after every apply-time write
row_cache_invalidation.definition: Invalidate rather than rebuild: a plugin whose read site falls through to a fresh read when its cache row is ABSENT needs the row deleted, not reconstructed, and needs no rebuild command to exist.

manifest_regenerator.title: a declared regenerator that rebuilds derived tables from applied authored state and fails loudly on a stale row
manifest_regenerator.definition: An always-on-write `regen_dependency` naming a regenerator file, for derived state where row EXISTENCE is not a sufficient postcondition because a present row can disagree with the authored state that was just applied.

row_cache_entry_invalidation.title: a per-row object-cache ENTRY invalidation, whose key or group carries the row id
row_cache_entry_invalidation.definition: A `tables.<t>.invalidate[]` verb naming one WordPress object-cache entry -- `{cache_group, cache_key}`, with `{id}` substituting the row's resolved local id into either member -- dropped and PROVEN gone after every apply-time write to that row. Distinct from `row_cache_invalidation`, which reaches a cache stored AS a database row (a table row or an option); no DELETE reaches the object cache. Admitted on TWO independent demands and not before: `manifests/providers/paid-memberships-pro-cache.php:92` puts the id on the key side, `manifests/providers/woocommerce-product-lookups.php:1301` puts it on the group side, and it is the second that made the rule '{id} in EITHER member' rather than a transcription of one plugin's spelling.

coordinates.cannot_represent: `wpforms` post content is a JSON document carrying cross-entity references inside it, and none of the three body modes addressed a declared path inside one — `blocks` runs a block parser over a document with no blocks, `serialized` decodes PHP serialization that is not there, `verbatim` preserves the source-local id, and omitting `body` defaults to `blocks`. THIS ROW'S EARLIER SENTENCE — "includes the form's source-local numeric `id`" — was measured WRONG on a live 2.0.0.5 pair on 2026-08-25: the top-level `id` is ABSENT on the template create path, an INT on the `['builder' => false]` path (includes/class-form.php:611-639), and a STRING on the real builder save, because includes/admin/ajax-actions.php:36-52 rebuilds the posted form from a flat jQuery input list so every leaf reaching update() is a string. The unambiguously cross-entity reference is `settings.confirmations.<n>.page`: a PAGE post id stored as a JSON STRING, on a key that also legitimately holds the literal `previous_page` (includes/class-process.php:1553-1562 branches on exactly that before `get_permalink((int) …)`).

Every `wpforms` post carries a `wpforms_form_locations` postmeta row: a PHP-serialized list of the posts that EMBED the form, each entry holding the embedding post's id, permalink path, and denormalized copies of its title and status. Read at the source it is unambiguously DERIVED rather than authored — `WPForms\Forms\Locator::hooks()` maintains it on `save_post`, `post_updated`, `wp_trash_post`, `untrash_post`, `delete_post`, `permalink_structure_changed` and three widget-option writes (src/Forms/Locator.php:203-216), and `FormsLocatorScanTask` rebuilds it in FULL from a REGEXP over `post_content` on a recurring `DAY_IN_SECONDS` schedule (src/Tasks/Actions/FormsLocatorScanTask.php:153, :184-186, :387). So `class: "derived"` represents it and it needs no new declarative primitive to capture. What is not representable is the apply-side postcondition: Duo writes `wp_posts` with a direct `Db::update()` (agent/src/Apply/PostMaterializer.php:229), so none of those eight hooks fires and a target's locations meta stays stale until the plugin's own scheduled scan next runs. A derivation that is scheduled rather than synchronous is exactly the bounded postcondition this primitive is about, and an exit code from a rebuild command would not prove it either. The 2026-08-22 pass could not have seen this coordinate: the row only exists once a form is actually embedded in a page and the locator scan has run, which a hand-written fixture never triggers.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: a bounded postcondition over the plugin's scheduled form-locations derivation

coordinates.cannot_represent: The `wpforms/form-selector` Gutenberg block persists `formId` as a JSON string. The current block-reference codec accepts `int|int[]` and writes an integer back, changing the stored type even if the identity resolves.
Forms also use the `wpforms_form_tag` taxonomy. A forms-only post-type draft omits authored plugin state.

candidates.closing: The block-selector coordinate closed in WP-6.1 (`attr_id_codecs`), the JSON body coordinate closed in WP-6.5 (`body_refs` plus the `json` body mode), and the taxonomy coordinate closed with the WP-6.6 exercise itself — `wpforms_form_tag` declared by the fixture adapter, its terms captured and applied on a live pair, and the `term:wpforms_form_tag` deletion contract (one guard, the one the feasibility report shows can lock; `term_taxonomy.parent` omitted because includes/class-form.php:136 registers the taxonomy non-hierarchical) reviewed into the authored certificate the suite signs. Only `post_meta.wpforms_form_locations`'s apply-side postcondition remains. WP-6.5 also corrected this row: the body coordinate's original one-sentence claim about a "source-local numeric `id`" was true for one of the plugin's three write paths and not for the common one, and the `wpforms_form_locations` coordinate was missing entirely because a hand-written fixture never produces it. Both were found by authoring the entities through WPForms' own APIs on a live pair rather than with `wp post create --post_content=…`, which is the discipline `docs/guides/adapter-authoring.md` § 1 already states and `sandbox/tests/grind/grind_adapter_walk.sh:582-586` does not follow. The WPForms site adapter in `docs/grind/adapter-walk.md` remains an authoring and trust-flow fixture only; it is not a platform support claim.

coordinates.cannot_represent: `redirection_items.action_data` can be a PHP-serialized array containing a target URL. Typed-table authored strings currently pass through `tokenize_text()` as opaque bytes. Replacing a source URL can change its byte length without updating PHP serialization length prefixes, producing invalid data on capture.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: structured typed-table column codecs that decode, tokenize string leaves, and re-encode canonical PHP serialization

coordinates.cannot_represent: Group/item raw writes also bypass `Red_Module::flush()`, so generated module state needs a bounded postcondition rather than an exit-code-only callback.

candidates.closing: The `action_data` coordinate closed in WP-6.1 — `sandbox/tests/offline/grammar/regress_column_codec_grammar.php` authors this candidate end to end as a `column_codecs` fixture adapter that validates, captures and round-trips. Capture is therefore representable; the module-flush postcondition is not, so no Redirection manifest is shipped and none would claim apply if it were.

coordinates.cannot_represent: `cptui_post_types` and `cptui_taxonomies` are nested authored arrays. The `menu_icon` field may be a site URL, but a plain array-valued option with no reference declaration does not currently tokenize nested string leaves.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: an explicit structured-leaf text codec independent of fake reference paths

coordinates.cannot_represent: Duo writes options after WordPress `init`; CPT UI registers its dynamic post types and taxonomies during `init`. Newly applied definitions therefore do not exist in the same process that would need them for entity materialization.

A taxonomy `default_term` produces `default_term_<taxonomy>` with a local term id. The option name is dynamic and the value is derived/reference-shaped; treating it as ordinary authored data would leak a local id.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: a generic dynamic derived option-name reference rule

candidates.closing: Until those exist, no CPT UI manifest is shipped.

coordinates.cannot_represent: typed rows and shortcode refs are representable, but direct table writes bypass the plugin's object-cache cleanup and optional flat-file execution rebuild. `manifests/code-snippets.json` therefore does not claim apply.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: a bounded postcondition over the plugin's object-cache cleanup and flat-file execution rebuild

coordinates.cannot_represent: Code Snippets' own cleanup drops `wp_cache_delete(Settings\CACHE_KEY, CACHE_GROUP)` (manifests/providers/code-snippets-state.php:94) -- one settings entry the whole `snippets` table shares, keyed by neither the row nor anything derived from it. WP-6.2's `{cache_group, cache_key}` verb requires `{id}` in one member, so a table-scoped entry still has no declarative spelling and this plugin's object cache stays reachable only through a provider.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: a table-scoped object-cache invalidation with somewhere engine-owned to live

coordinates.cannot_represent: both route slugs are representable, but the plugin's own settings path flushes rewrite rules. A clean-target request matrix must establish the required postcondition before apply is claimed.
coordinates.remedy_phrase: a clean-target request matrix establishing the rewrite-flush postcondition

coordinates.cannot_represent: `pmpro_memberships_pages` and `pmpro_memberships_categories` are pure join tables: a two-column composite primary key, every identity column a reference, and no scalar row id at all. `identity.mode` admitted only `mapped` and `natural_key`, both of which require a scalar `pk`, so the membership-to-page and membership-to-category relationships stayed honest-intent markers in the manifest rather than declarations.

candidates.closing: Closed in DUO-3235 together with the `id_column` meta-table gap from the same round.

coordinates.cannot_represent: A shipping zone method stores its settings in an option whose NAME embeds the local zone-method row id (`woocommerce_<method>_<id>_settings`). Options were addressable only by literal name -- the `options` section is an exact whitelist and `option_patterns` drove no discovery scan -- so an option whose name carries a local reference could be neither discovered nor rebound, and shipping zones had no engine path at all.

candidates.closing: Closed in task #93, which graduated shipping zones and tax rates from an intent marker to a declared surface.

coordinates.cannot_represent: Ninja Forms caches a form's settings and fields in `nf3_upgrades` plus a legacy `nf_form_<id>` option. An apply-time write to a form's own row left that cache stale, so an id-reused form silently served the PREVIOUS form's settings. The grammar could express the row write but not the derived state the plugin's own save path drops, and Ninja Forms ships no rebuild command (`wp help nf` fails) for an exit-code callback to shell out to.

candidates.closing: Closed by reading Ninja Forms' own read site rather than by trial: `ModelFactory` falls through to a fresh `nf3_forms`/`nf3_fields` read the moment the cache row is ABSENT, which is why invalidation is sufficient and a rebuilder was not required to close the gap.

coordinates.cannot_represent: The Events Calendar keeps every event's dates in the derived custom tables `tec_events`/`tec_occurrences`, which capture excludes. Row EXISTENCE was the only postcondition the grammar could state, and an adopted target event can already hold a `tec_occurrences` row whose dates disagree with the applied post meta -- a present-but-stale row that an existence check passes.

candidates.closing: Closed in DUO-3234 plus the 2026-08-22 production-readiness stale-row regression; the existence check remains as the generic backstop underneath the regenerator.

coordinates.cannot_represent: PMPro reads membership-level metadata through get_metadata(), which caches per level id in the `pmpro_membership_level_meta` object-cache group. Duo writes `pmpro_membership_levelmeta` by SQL and fires none of the metadata API's invalidation, so an applied level served its PRE-APPLY meta for as long as that entry lived. `invalidate[]` could delete a table row or an option row but had no verb for an object-cache ENTRY, so the whole repair had to be hook code: one action, one `providers[].source: "manifest"` row, and a provider whose entire product act is wp_cache_delete() in a loop -- which alone held the adapter at `compatibility_shim`.

candidates.closing: Closed in WP-6.2 by generalising the verb rather than by adopting PMPro's spelling: WooCommerce's `object_<id>`/`lookup_table` drop (manifests/providers/woocommerce-product-lookups.php:1301) is the second independent demand and puts the id on the GROUP side, so the admitted rule is `{id}` in EITHER member. The engine proves the drop with a wp_cache_get() readback, matching the refusal the provider it replaces already raised (paid-memberships-pro-cache.php:96-99) -- an unverified delete would have shipped the stale read in a shorter spelling. The SHIPPED manifest is deliberately not restamped: a byte under manifests/ is adapter identity (AGENTS.md rule 2), so the declarative form is demonstrated on a synthetic fixture derived from those bytes at runtime.
